textbookText: Ans:- Element X has three electrons in its outermost orbit because element X is placed in Group IIIA of the modern periodic
table. All elements of Group IIIA possess three valence electrons in their outermost shell.
ii) In a chemical reaction, some element donate electrons and some receive. In a chemical reaction between X and Y, which
is likely to receive electrons and which donates electrons? Justify your answer.
Ans:- Ina chemical reaction between X and Y, X donates electron and Y receives electrons because element X belongs to
Group IIIA and has only three valence electrons, so it tends to lose electrons to attain stability. Element Y belongs to Group
VIIA and has seven valence electrons, so it tends to gain one electron to complete its octet and become stable.
iii) What happens to the reactivity of elements when moving top to bottom in the group containing elements X and Y? why?
Ans:- In the group containing X (Group IIIA), the reactivity increases from top to bottom. And In the group containing Y
(Group VIIA), the reactivity decreases from top to bottom. Because down a group, atomic size increases. In metals like
Group IIIA, increased atomic size makes the loss of valence electrons easier, so reactivity increases. In non-metals like Group
VIIA, increased atomic size reduces the tendency to gain electrons, so reactivity decreases.
4. Element ‘A’ has valency 2 and it falls in s-block of the periodic table. Element B has valency 1 and falls in p-block of
the periodic table.
i) What type of bond is formed when elements A and B combine? How?
Ans:- An ionic (electrovalent) bond is formed because element A (s-block metal) loses two electrons to attain a stable
configuration, while two atoms of element B (p-block non-metal) each gain one electron. The transfer of electrons produces
oppositely charged ions, and the electrostatic attraction between them results in an ionic bond.
ii) What type of bond is formed when two atoms of element B combine? How?
Ans:- A covalent bond is formed because both atoms of element B are non-metals and have the same tendency to gain
electrons. Instead of electron transfer, they share one pair of electrons to complete their outermost shells, forming a covalent
bond.
iii) Compare chemical reactivity of element A with the element having atomic number 1 less than it.
Ans:- Element A is less reactive than the element with atomic number 1 less than it because A belongs to Group 2 and
requires more energy to lose two valence electrons than the Group 1 element (to its left) requires to lose just one.
5. Electronic configuration of some elements are as given below:
i) Write the group and the block of the most reactive metal among these.
Ans:- The most reactive metal is element Y (2,8,2) its group is IIA and Block is s-block.
ii) Write the valency of the elements X and Z.
Ans:- The valency of the elements X and Z are 3 and 4 respectively.
iii) Explain the position of element W in the modern periodic table.
Ans:- Element W (2, 8, 5) has five electrons in its outermost shell, so it is placed in Group 15 (VA group).
Since its last electron enters a p-orbital, it belongs to the p-block.

ii) Which one is more reactive, F or Cl, why?
Ans:- F (Fluorine) is more reactive than Cl (Chlorine) because it has a smaller atomic size. This smaller radius allows its
nucleus to exert a stronger force of attraction on incoming electrons, making it easier for Fluorine to gain an electron and
complete its octet compared to Chlorine.
iii) Write a balanced chemical equation between the element of this group belonging to 3rd period and an element of IIA
group.
Ans:- The element in the 3rd period of this group is Chlorine (Cl). A common element from Group IIA (Alkaline Earth
Metals) is Magnesium (Mg).
